topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture topic and outlines the expected learning outcomes for understanding cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional modalities: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss traditional cancer treatment approaches that eliminate tumor tissue physically or damage dividing cells systemically.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic tumor vulnerabilities and DNA repair defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine therapeutic strategies that take advantage of specific tumor weaknesses such as hormone dependence, checkpoint loss, and synthetic lethality.

topics.label: Targeting oncogenic kinase signaling and therapeutic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore small molecule kinase inhibitors targeted against oncogene addiction alongside the molecular mechanisms of treatment resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapies and targeted drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the design and application of monoclonal antibodies used either alone to engage immune effector mechanisms or linked to deliver cytotoxic drugs.

topics.label: Immune surveillance and T-cell-directed immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the immune system interacts with tumors and how immune checkpoint inhibitors, BiTEs, and CAR T cells mobilize T-cell responses.

topics.label: Overarching challenges, historical progress, and future directions in oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on key clinical challenges in cancer therapy, survival improvements over recent decades, and future strategies for disease management.
